## On-Call Handoff — Gateway 503s

**Status:** Ongoing (unresolved as of last log entry, 2026-03-14T03:29:33.942Z)

**Root cause:**
Deploy `dep-4471` (gateway, a.novak, "config: connection-per-request for pool isolation") applied config generation 119 at 02:13:41Z, flipping `gateway.pool.perRequest: false -> true`. This made every request claim its own DB connection instead of sharing the pool. The fixed pool size (20) saturated almost immediately, so requests queue for a connection and time out (~660-720ms) before returning 503.

**Error signature:**
```
ERROR pool req-XXXXX ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool (size 20, in_use 20, waiting N)
```
`waiting` climbs continuously (13 → 238+ by 03:29) — the backlog is not draining, so it will not self-heal.

**Impact window:**
- Deploy shipped: 2026-03-14T02:12:00Z–02:14:00Z
- First WARN (slow acquire): 02:14:14.920Z
- First 503: **02:14:18.972Z**
- Still failing and backlog growing at log end: 03:29:33.942Z (>1h15m elapsed, no recovery)

**Scope:** Gateway only — confirmed `worker.log` clean for this window (no errors, only an unrelated pre-existing slow-query WARN at 02:36 tied to known issue OPS-2210). Downstream services (billing/orders/catalog/accounts-svc) are not the cause; the gateway is exhausting connections to all of them.

**Action: roll back `dep-4471`** — revert `gateway.pool.perRequest` to `false` (config generation 119 → prior). This is the only change correlated with onset; no other deploy in `deploys.csv` falls in the window.
